title: Build tiered SLO config schema + validation tooling (CI checks)
creator: Aisha Bello
description:
Problem:
We’re formalizing tiered SLOs (Hosted vs Dedicated) and need a canonical, machine-readable configuration that can drive:
- SLO dashboards (Console + Grafana)
- Burn-rate alert rules + recording rules
- Error budget computation jobs
- Deploy gate policy (warn-only -> enforced)

Today, SLO targets live in docs/spreadsheets and are easy to drift from actual SLI definitions/metric coverage. We also need guardrails so new endpoints/regions don’t ship without SLO coverage, and so config changes are reviewed/validated consistently.

Scope:
1) Define a config schema for SLO definitions per tier + endpoint class + region (and where required, per deployment-mode tag).
2) Implement validation tooling:
   - Schema validation (shape + types)
   - Semantic validation (allowed values, windows, objective ranges, tier/region rules)
   - Metric coverage validation (required SLI metrics exist for each SLO definition)
3) Add CI checks in redwood + slo-toolkit to block merge on invalid config or missing metric coverage (with an allowlisted escape hatch for early rollout).

Out of scope:
- Final SLO target negotiation (tracked in PM-812)
- Tier tagging at ingress/routing (ENG-4922)
- Burn-rate alert query implementation (ENG-4930)

Primary owners/stakeholders:
- SRE: Aisha Bello, Rafael Mendes
- Telemetry: Logan Wright, Thomas Baird
- Deploy gates: Jordan Lee, Connor O'Brien
- Routing/SLI boundaries: Mina Haddad, Allison Grant

Deliverable:
A versioned SLO config schema + CLI validator + CI integration, used as the source of truth for tiered SLOs across Hosted and Dedicated.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Config schema exists in-repo and is versioned (supports additive evolution without breaking existing configs).
2) A validator can run locally and in CI and produces actionable errors (file path + line + remediation hints).
3) Config supports at minimum:
   - tier: hosted|dedicated
   - endpoint_class: chat|completions|embeddings|rerank
   - transport: unary|streaming (streaming required for chat/completions)
   - region: us-east|us-west|eu-west (initial set; must be enum)
   - slis: success_rate, latency_p{50,95,99}, streaming_disconnect_rate
   - objective + rolling_window
   - explicit exclusions / filters (invalid_request, rate_limited, client_abort)
4) Semantic validation:
   - objective ranges enforced (0 < objective <= 1)
   - latency SLOs require a percentile and a threshold in ms
   - streaming SLOs only allowed when transport=streaming
   - dedicated configs require a customer_scope field (account|pool) and must not default to global shared measurements
5) Metric coverage validation:
   - For every SLO entry, required metric names/labels exist in the metrics catalog (or can be discovered via Prometheus label/series check in staging)
   - Validation fails if tier/region labels are missing in the metric spec
6) CI integration:
   - PR touching slo-config/ must run validator and fail hard on errors
   - Warn-only mode available via repo flag for the first rollout week; warns must still post to PR checks
7) Docs:
   - README describing schema fields, examples for Hosted + Dedicated, and common failure modes
   - Link to Confluence SLI standard and error budget policy doc
implementation_notes:
Proposed structure:
- Store configs under: infra/slo-config/v1/*.yaml (one file per tier or per endpoint class; keep diffs readable)
- Provide JSONSchema/OpenAPI-style schema: infra/slo-config/schema/v1.schema.json
- Provide CLI tool: ./tools/sloctl validate --path infra/slo-config/v1

Schema shape (high level):
- apiVersion: slo.redwood.ai/v1
- kind: SLOConfig
- metadata: name, owner_team, last_reviewed
- spec:
  - tier: hosted|dedicated
  - region: us-east|us-west|eu-west
  - endpoint_class: chat|completions|embeddings|rerank
  - transport: unary|streaming
  - reporting_window: 28d (fixed for now)
  - slis:
    - success_rate:
        objective: 0.999
        numerator: requests_total{result="success"}
        denominator: requests_total{exclude_reason=""}
        exclusions: ["invalid_request","rate_limited","client_abort"]
    - latency:
        objective_p95_ms: 1200
        objective_p99_ms: 2500
        measurement: end_to_end (gateway->last_token for streaming; gateway->response for unary)
    - streaming:
        disconnect_objective: 0.999
        disconnect_event: stream_terminated_total{reason!="client_abort"}

Important: Config should reference a metrics catalog identifier rather than embedding raw PromQL everywhere.
- Add a small registry (metrics-catalog.yaml) that maps SLI primitive names -> canonical metric names + required labels.
- Validator checks config references valid catalog entries + required labels (tier, region, endpoint_class).

Cardinality control:
- Do not allow per-model or per-customer dimensions in the SLO config directly.
- Dedicated: allow customer_scope=account for the dashboard views, but SLO computation should rely on a bounded label set (account_id allowed only in Dedicated dashboards, not in global SLO burn calculations unless we pre-aggregate).
- Validation should fail if a config introduces disallowed labels (model_id, prompt_hash, request_id).

CI design:
- GitHub action step runs sloctl validate.
- For metric coverage, run in two modes:
  - static mode: validate against metrics-catalog.yaml (fast, runs on every PR)
  - optional integration mode: validate against staging Prometheus (nightly or manually triggered) to avoid flakes.

Open question to resolve in review:
- Do we encode streaming SLO as disconnect_rate OR successful_stream_completion_rate? (Allison leaning to completion rate for easier accounting; Aisha leaning to disconnects because it matches customer reports).

comments: 2026-01-10 (Aisha Bello): Please prioritize “validator output quality” (clear error messages, pointers). If this is painful we won’t get adoption and folks will keep editing spreadsheets.

2026-01-14 (Logan Wright): Strong preference to reference a metrics catalog vs embedding PromQL in config. We can generate recording rules from stable metric primitives and keep queries consistent across tiers.

2026-01-16 (Allison Grant): For streaming accounting, exclude client aborts explicitly (client closed connection) and invalid requests. Do not exclude server-side timeouts; those must count against SLO even if retry succeeded downstream.

2026-01-22 (Jordan Lee): Deploy gate will call a “budget state” endpoint, but we still want CI to block invalid config edits before they affect budget jobs. Add a required field: spec.owner_team so we can route review/pings.

2026-01-27 (Thomas Baird): Add a linter rule: disallow high-cardinality labels in any SLO computation path. In particular, allow account_id only for Dedicated customer dashboards, not for alerting SLO rollups.

2026-02-03 (Sahana Iyer): I’ll land schema + validator first, then wire CI. Metric coverage integration to staging Prometheus should be optional to avoid flakes; propose nightly job that reports drift in Slack.

2026-02-12 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure schema supports multiple latency objectives in one SLO (p95+p99). Also, enforce 28d window for error budget accounting in v1 to reduce ambiguity; we can generalize later.
